# Feather

> Agent memory in a single file. An embedded vector database with memory
> semantics — adaptive decay, trust levels, confidence, scoped working sets and
> context packets — that runs inside your agent process. No server, no daemon,
> no network hop. `pip install feather-db`.

Feather is not a general-purpose database and does not try to be. It has no
transactions, no query planner, and one writer per file. It is built for one
job: being the thing an agent remembers into.

## Install

```bash
pip install feather-db          # Python, binary wheels for cp39-cp314
cargo install feather-db-cli    # Rust CLI
docker pull ghcr.io/feather-store/feather-api
```

## The 30-second version

```python
import feather_db, numpy as np
db = feather_db.DB.open("memory.feather", dim=768)

meta = feather_db.Metadata()
meta.content = "user prefers written async updates"
meta.namespace_id = "org.user_842.preferences"
meta.confidence = 0.9
db.add(id=1, vec=embedding, meta=meta)

db.search(query_vec, k=5)            # vector
db.keyword_search("async", k=5)      # BM25, Porter-stemmed
db.hybrid_search(query_vec, "async") # reciprocal rank fusion
db.close()                           # releases the file lock
```

## What makes it a memory engine rather than a vector store

- **Adaptive decay** — `stickiness = 1 + ln(1 + recall_count)`; frequently
  recalled memories age more slowly. Relevance, validity and importance are
  separate fields, never collapsed.
- **Trust and confidence** — `confidence` (how likely a record is true) is a
  distinct axis from `importance` (how much it matters), and both are
  filterable.
- **Scoped working sets** — `Pocket` gives each agent a budget-fitted hot set
  over dotted, inheriting scopes, with warm storage behind it.
- **Context packets** — required constraints are resolved first and the packet
  **fails closed** if one cannot be found, so a brand rule can never be silently
  dropped to make room.
- **Single file** — one `.feather` on disk. Copy it, back it up, delete it.

## Honest limits

- One writer process per file; a second is refused by name, not queued. Readers
  are unlimited and lock-free, seeing a consistent snapshot as of their open.
- No transactions and no query planner.
- Prefiltered ANN is metadata equality, not graph traversal.
- BM25 is Porter-stemmed, which handles plurals and verb forms but not every
  derivational pair. Anything relying on paraphrase needs a real embedder.
- Format v9; bitemporal fields (`valid_from` / `observed_at`) are not yet in the
  record and are planned for v10.

## Benchmarks

LongMemEval (ICLR 2025), 500 questions, retrieval recall:

| metric | BM25, no embedder |
| --- | --- |
| recall@1 | 0.874 |
| recall@3 | 0.942 |
| recall@5 | 0.974 |
| recall@10 | 0.986 |

11 seconds end to end on a laptop, no API key. Reproduce with
`python benchmarks/longmemeval.py --data lme_s.json --mode keyword`.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/feather-store/feather/blob/master/README.md): full API
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/feather-store/feather/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md): every release, including the defects each one fixed
- [Technical reference](https://github.com/feather-store/feather/blob/master/CLAUDE.md): architecture, file format, gotchas — written for coding agents
- [Storage spec](https://github.com/feather-store/feather/blob/master/docs/singularity-storage-spec.md): sizing, compaction, backup, measured numbers

## Integrations

- **MCP** — `feather-agent` exposes memory to Claude Desktop and Claude Code as
  5 tools, 3 prompts and 2 resources.
- **LangGraph** — `FeatherStore` is a `BaseStore`, so it is long-term,
  cross-thread agent memory in one line: `builder.compile(store=FeatherStore(...))`.
- **Cloud API** — optional FastAPI server when you want it over HTTP instead of
  in-process.
